spec.description: Citi Bike's network of stations on an average weekday or weekend day of September 2026: where the bikes leave from and pile up in each hour, the busiest links between parts of the city, and the bikes left out of place. Drag across the hours to see the morning rush turn around in the evening; draw an area to follow it.

options.content:
### About the data

- **Trips**: Citi Bike's [system data](https://citibikenyc.com/system-data) (Lyft), September 2026: 4.97 million
  trips in New York between two stations (dockless e-bike trips left out). Jersey City and Hoboken publish their
  own files: their stations appear only where trips from New York ended.
- **An average day**: a month's counts divided by its 21 working days (Weekday) or its 9 Saturdays, Sundays and
  Labor Day (Weekend). A bike counts out in the hour its trip started and in in the hour it ended, New York time.
- **Links** join H3 cells of about 0.7 km² (resolution 8): station to station, trips are too thin to draw.

Built by `datasets/citibike/build.sh` in pacha-dashboards, from any month.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT name AS "Station", round(o) AS "Out", round(i) AS "In", round(i - o) AS "Balance"
FROM (SELECT name, sum(bikes_out) AS o, sum(bikes_in) AS i FROM $hourly WHERE day = $day AND $__crossfilter($bikeFilters) GROUP BY name) ORDER BY i - o ASC LIMIT 8

spec.rawSql:
-- Each station in the hours kept, on the day picked (the area drawn on this map left out, so every station
-- stays): bikes taken out and brought in on an average day, and the balance. Orange stations empty (more bikes
-- leave than arrive), blue ones fill; the larger the dot, the more bikes the hours leave out of place there.
-- The filters name bare columns: they go on $hourly alone, before the join.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT name, sum(bikes_out) AS o, sum(bikes_in) AS i FROM $hourly
  WHERE day = $day AND $__crossfilter($bikeFilters, -area) GROUP BY name
)
SELECT s.name, s.latitude, s.longitude, round(b.o, 1) AS bikes_out, round(b.i, 1) AS bikes_in,
       round(b.i - b.o, 1) AS balance, abs(b.i - b.o) AS out_of_place,
       -- the colour: the balance as a share of the station's traffic, -60 % (emptying) to +60 % (filling)
       greatest(-0.6, least(0.6, (b.i - b.o) / (b.i + b.o))) AS colour
FROM b JOIN $stations s USING (name)
WHERE b.i + b.o >= 1
ORDER BY out_of_place

-- The busiest links between parts of the city in the hours kept, on the day picked: trips between H3 cells of
-- about 0.7 km² on an average day, summed over the hours. The 300 busiest, drawn as animated arcs, wider and
-- faster the more trips they carry. The hour filter names the bare column hour, which $links has too.
WITH l AS (
  SELECT cell0, cell1, any_value(lat0) AS lat0, any_value(lng0) AS lng0, any_value(lat1) AS lat1,
         any_value(lng1) AS lng1, sum(trips) AS trips
  FROM $links WHERE day = $day AND $__crossfilter($bikeFilters, -area)
  GROUP BY cell0, cell1
)
SELECT lat0, lng0, lat1, lng1, round(trips) AS trips FROM l ORDER BY trips DESC LIMIT 300

The arcs are the busiest links between parts of the city (H3 cells of about 0.7 km²). Draw an area to keep its stations in the figures.

spec.rawSql: SELECT sum(greatest(i - o, 0)) AS "Bikes" FROM (SELECT name, sum(bikes_out) AS o, sum(bikes_in) AS i FROM $hourly WHERE day = $day AND $__crossfilter($bikeFilters) GROUP BY name)

spec.description: Over the hours kept, the bikes that pile up at the stations that gain more than they lose: what Citi Bike's trucks and its Bike Angels have to carry back for the system to stay in balance.

spec.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS "Stations" FROM (SELECT name, sum(bikes_out) AS o, sum(bikes_in) AS i FROM $hourly WHERE day = $day AND $__crossfilter($bikeFilters) GROUP BY name) WHERE o + i >= 1

options.content:
### How New York's bike share breathes

Citi Bike is a network of some 2,400 stations and the trips between them: about **180,000 on an average weekday**
of September 2026. Each trip takes a bike from one dock and leaves it at another.

**Breathe in.** From 7 to 10 in the morning the bikes leave the East Village, the Lower East Side, Hell's Kitchen,
Brooklyn and Queens, and pile up around Penn Station and Grand Central, in Hudson Square and at the Brooklyn Navy
Yard: some **8,000 bikes**, one trip in four, end up where they are not wanted.

**Breathe out.** From 5 in the evening the flow turns around, and by midnight the city has given almost all of them
back: over the whole day only 1,500 end up out of place. On a weekend there is no rush to undo.

Drag across the hours in the chart and watch the city fill and empty; draw an area on the map to follow one part.

spec.title: How New York's bike share breathes: Citi Bike hour by hour

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: Citi Bike's stations in the month, by name as the trips give it, placed at the median of the
-- trips' coordinates there, with the trips that started and ended there (datasets/citibike in pacha-dashboards).
SELECT name, latitude, longitude, trips_out, trips_in
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/citibike/stations.parquet')

spec.description: Bikes out and in at each station, hour by hour, on an average day.
spec.label: Hourly
spec.name: hourly

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: for each station, kind of day (Weekday, or Weekend with the holidays) and hour of the day (New York
-- time), the bikes taken out and brought in on an average day of that kind; with the station's place, so that an
-- area drawn on the map can keep its stations.
SELECT h.name, h.day, h.hour::INTEGER AS hour, h.bikes_out, h.bikes_in, s.latitude, s.longitude
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/citibike/hourly.parquet') h
JOIN read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/citibike/stations.parquet') s USING (name)

spec.description: The busiest links between parts of the city, hour by hour, on an average day.
spec.label: Links
spec.name: links

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: trips between H3 cells of about 0.7 km² (resolution 8) on an average day of each kind, by hour of
-- departure: the 400 busiest pairs of cells in each hour, with the cells' centres.
SELECT day, hour::INTEGER AS hour, cell0, cell1, lat0, lng0, lat1, lng1, trips
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/citibike/links.parquet')

spec.description: An average working day, or an average Saturday, Sunday or holiday.
